name: Security dilemma
short: One state arms or allies to feel safe. Its neighbor reads that as preparation for attack and answers in kind. Defensive intentions produce a spiral neither side wanted.

name: Private information
short: Each side hides its strength or exaggerates its resolve. Because neither can see the other's true bottom line, both demand more than the other will accept.

name: Commitment problem
short: A deal that works today cannot be enforced tomorrow. A state that expects to grow weaker fights now rather than trust a rising rival to keep its word.

name: Misperception
short: Leaders underestimate resistance, misread intentions, or assume an ally will come. The error makes a ruinous war look short and manageable.

name: Leaders' domestic incentives
short: The costs of war fall on society; the costs of backing down fall on the leader. When survival in office is at stake, the leader's calculation diverges from the country's.

name: Issues treated as indivisible
short: Sovereignty, sacred ground, or national identity get framed so that splitting the difference is politically impossible.

name: Alliance entanglement
short: A state joins a war it did not start because an ally's defeat would leave it exposed. This is the mechanism that turns a local war into a wide one.

name: Power transition
short: A rising challenger approaches a declining leader. The leader is tempted to fight before it is overtaken; the challenger is tempted to fight once it can win.

name: Steps to war
short: A territorial dispute hardens into a rivalry, rivalry brings alliances and arms racing, and repeated crises teach both sides that the next one will be decided by force.

name: State weakness
short: Where the state cannot police its territory, armed groups can recruit, hide, and survive. Diversity alone does not predict civil war; weak capacity does.
